findings.where: Destination cards (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok), both the uppercase region label and the place-name title, at desktop and phone
findings.fault: The cards are set in a monospace typewriter face. The brand uses only Quicksand and Nunito Sans, and card titles should be Quicksand 600. The page now has a third typeface, which reads like code or placeholder text, and it clashes with the rounded Quicksand heading right above it.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the brand sheet fixes the two typefaces and Quicksand for card titles. A backpacker would also find these the only clinical, sterile-looking parts of a beachy page, on the very cards that lead to the guides.

findings.where: 'Where we're starting' section heading, against the hero's MantaHostels h1, worst at desktop
findings.fault: The section h2 is set far larger than the page's h1. At desktop it is about twice the height of the hero title and takes two huge lines. The size order is upside down: a secondary section heading shouts over the hero that says what the site is, and it dwarfs the three small cards it introduces.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor reading the size order. They would take the heading of a list of three places as the main message, while the hero's name and claim look smaller than it. The brand's rule is loud moments in the hero and calm below it.

findings.where: Hero intro paragraph ('We're building a search that ranks…'), at desktop
findings.fault: The hero's one explanatory paragraph is set at small body size, close to footer text, right under a very large display title. It looks like fine print rather than the plain mechanics that should back the claim, and the jump from display size to this paragraph skips any lead size.
findings.who_objects: A visitor deciding what Manta is. The sentence that explains the product is the easiest thing in the hero to skip. The rules file asks for the calm half to sit plainly beneath the loud claim and make it credible, not to disappear under it.

findings.where: Desktop nav links, 'Destinations' and 'How we rank'
findings.fault: Two side-by-side nav links are set differently: 'How we rank' is underlined and 'Destinations' is not. Neither one is the current page, so the difference means nothing. If anything, it is the reverse of the house convention, where the current-page link drops its underline for semibold.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning the nav could read the underlined link as the current page or as a different kind of link. The founder would object because like items should be set alike and the nav rule is specified.
